more_info.banned_in:
Approved in the EU.
Approved in the US.
US food use is subject to the listed CFR provisions and their conditions, checked in 2026.
more_info.overview: Ammonia caramel is a brown carbohydrate-derived colour made using ammonium compounds, without sulphites in the caramelisation process. It is used to add colour or restore colour lost during food manufacture. Made by heating food-grade carbohydrates with ammonium compounds. Sulphite compounds are excluded from this class. The specified material is supplied as deep brown liquid or solid.
more_info.uses:
Examples in the EU food-use list include certain other confectionery including breath freshening microsweets; chewing gum; decorations, coatings and fillings, except fruit-based fillings covered by category 4.2.4; flavoured drinks; flavoured fermented milk products including heat-treated products; unripened cheese excluding products falling in category 16.
The entries apply to particular food categories and may limit the amount, the preparation or the way it is used; they do not show how often the additive appears in retail products.
more_info.daily_intake: 300 mg/kg body weight/day, combined caramel colours (EFSA, 2011). Within that group limit, E150c has a separate limit of 100 mg/kg body weight/day.
more_info.origin: Made by heating food-grade carbohydrates with ammonium compounds. Sulphite compounds are excluded from this class.
more_info.side_effects:
EFSA identified uncertainties about manufacturing contaminants in 2011.
High-exposure estimates could exceed the group limit.
